A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ECHOMIST study and provide readable main text, figures, tables and Appendices A–F. Moved and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 15 LLMs, including misinformation responses, factual-knowledge tests and mitigation experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds claim-falsity subgroup results, retrieval-agent comparisons and RAG case studies.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, Self-Alert procedure and RAG pipeline remain unchanged, including their prompts. Retrieval Agents in Appendix D.3 is an additional cited comparison method.

E1.justification: Both retain the same 2,691 ECHOMIST queries, three data sources, 3,456-question factual-knowledge test and true-premise query evaluation. The new partial-versus-entirely-false analysis partitions existing coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Appendix D.3/Table 8 adds Retrieval Agents from Tian et al. (2024) alongside no mitigation, Self-Alert and RAG for Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.1-70B and GPT-4. The principal 15-model roster remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 Section 4.2 introduces a subgroup comparison using Snopes labels: mostly false, mixture and unproven constitute partially false claims, versus false for entirely false claims. Existing zero-shot procedures, metrics, judge selection and decoding budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds the claim-falsity subgroup analysis, two RAG success/failure cases in Figure 7, and source-specific query-prefix distributions in Figure 8, replacing the word-cloud analysis. Existing temporal, knowledge, query-type, source and topic analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain the 70-query, two-annotator judge validation, the same reported correlations, dataset dispersion statistics and entropy/Spearman analysis. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports partial/entirely-false scores, including 26.3%/35.9% for Qwen-2.5-72B. Table 8 adds Retrieval Agents scores of 25.85%, 34.65% and 42.45% for Llama-3.1-8B/70B and GPT-4. Some newly tabulated existing-method results differ from retained Figure 6: GPT-4 Self-Alert is 46.36% in Table 8 versus approximately 45.3% plotted, without an explained setting change.

T1.justification: The scoring definitions, factual-knowledge test construction and entropy/correlation reasoning are retained. Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark novelty, model-vulnerability, insufficient-factual-knowledge and mitigation claims. The added analyses do not redefine the principal contributions.

C2.justification: v3 interprets poorer results on partially false claims as an ambiguity-related reliability limitation. Appendix D.3 additionally argues that advanced retrieval remains insufficient and motivates specialized mitigation. Existing explanations and limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices B, C and F retain the model identifiers, A40 hardware, temperatures, token limits and prompt templates. Code availability and restricted social-media data access instructions are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Liu et al. (2024a), X-eval, and Liu et al. (2024b), Holistic Evaluation for Interleaved Text-and-Image Generation, as evaluation references, plus Tian et al. (2024) for Retrieval Agents. Its positioning against CREPE and FalseQA remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited wording and acknowledgement edits, adds a Section 4.2 discussion and Appendix D.3, removes the word-cloud explanation and updates cross-references. The overall section order and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 4 and 8 and the RAG case figure, and replaces v2 Figure 7’s word cloud with the query-prefix chart. Other charts are retained; the judgment examples and evaluation prompts are relocated within the appendices.

improvement.justification: The subgroup analysis, RAG cases and additional retrieval comparison provide useful evidence about failure modes. However, new Table 8 contains unreconciled differences from retained Figure 6, and Appendix D.3 overgeneralizes Retrieval Agents’ gains over Self-Alert: GPT-4 scores 42.45% versus 46.36% in Table 8. These benefits and new reporting problems leave the net quality change unclear.
